sections.overview: Eumorpha labruscae, the gaudy sphinx, is a congener of E. anchemolus and E. fasciatus, described in their profiles.
sections.identification: The forewings are deep gray-green and the hindwings show purple-blue patches, yellow borders and a red spot; wingspan is 11–12 cm.
sections.habitat: Its range extends from Argentina through Central America and the Caribbean to the southern United States; northern records may be strays.
sections.diet: Larvae use grape-family vines including Vitis and Cissus; adults probably feed on flower nectar.
sections.behavior: Adults are thought to take nectar, while larvae pupate in shallow underground burrows.
sections.reproduction: Caterpillars pupate in shallow chambers or burrows in the soil; detailed egg-laying schedules are not summarized in the sources used.
sections.ecology: The three profiles are congeners, but their recorded larval hosts differ: this species uses the plant groups described above.
sections.conservation: BAMONA reports a globally secure category, though the species can be uncommon near range margins.
